title: Make dated incremental backups with rsync and keep only the newest copies
summary: Each run saves a full-looking copy of a folder into a new dated snapshot. Files that did not change are shared with the previous snapshot, so each copy takes little extra space. Old snapshots beyond the chosen number are removed.

aliases.text: rsync dated backups delete old ones

Dry run: show what would be copied without creating a snapshot. Nothing is written to the backup folder and nothing is deleted.

warnings: The script deletes every dated folder in DEST_ROOT beyond the KEEP newest. Keep only snapshots in that folder.
Hard links do not work on exFAT or FAT32 drives, which many external drives use. Use ext4 or btrfs for the backup drive.
A snapshot on the same disk does not protect against disk failure. Copy the backup drive somewhere else too.

script.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# Incremental snapshot backup. Each run creates a new dated folder. Files that did not
# change are hard links to the previous snapshot, so every snapshot looks complete but
# costs only the changed data. Snapshots beyond KEEP are deleted (oldest first).
# Usage: backup-rotate.sh SRC_DIR DEST_ROOT [KEEP] [--dry-run]
SRC="${1:?usage: $0 SRC_DIR DEST_ROOT [KEEP] [--dry-run]}"
DEST="${2:?usage: $0 SRC_DIR DEST_ROOT [KEEP] [--dry-run]}"
KEEP="${3:-7}"
DRY="${4:-}"
SNAP_RE='^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}_[0-9]{6}$'

[[ -d "$SRC" ]] || { echo "source folder not found: $SRC" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ "$KEEP" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { echo "KEEP must be a positive number" >&2; exit 1; }
if [[ "$DRY" != "--dry-run" ]]; then
  mkdir -p "$DEST"
fi
if [[ -d "$DEST" ]]; then
  DEST="$(cd "$DEST" && pwd -P)"   # absolute path, needed by --link-dest
fi
NEW="$DEST/$(date +%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S)"

# Link unchanged files to the newest snapshot, if there is one.
LINK=()
if [[ -e "$DEST/latest" ]]; then
  LINK=(--link-dest="$DEST/latest")
fi

if [[ "$DRY" == "--dry-run" ]]; then
  echo "DRY RUN: would create $NEW"
  rsync -aH --dry-run --stats ${LINK[@]+"${LINK[@]}"} "$SRC/" "$NEW/"
  exit 0
fi

rsync -aH --stats ${LINK[@]+"${LINK[@]}"} "$SRC/" "$NEW/"

# Point "latest" at the new snapshot; rename makes the switch atomic.
ln -sfn "$NEW" "$DEST/latest.tmp"
mv -Tf "$DEST/latest.tmp" "$DEST/latest"

# Rotation: keep the newest KEEP snapshots, delete the rest.
mapfile -t SNAPS < <(find "$DEST" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -printf '%f\n' | grep -E "$SNAP_RE" | sort)
COUNT=${#SNAPS[@]}
if (( COUNT > KEEP )); then
  for name in "${SNAPS[@]:0:COUNT-KEEP}"; do
    echo "removing old snapshot: $name"
    rm -rf -- "$DEST/$name"
  done
fi
echo "done: $NEW (snapshots kept: $(( COUNT > KEEP ? KEEP : COUNT )))"
